Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

don’t! phrase

telling someone not to

also do not!, don’t …!, mind you don’t, never …!, don’t look around

classical

Jo. 6, 20: Ego sum, nōlīte timēre.
Quint. 6.3.59: nōlī, inquit, tamquam assem elephantō dēs

nōlī, nōlīte (+ infinitive)

imperative of nōlō with an infinitive

don’t …!

The everyday prohibition of prose, gentle in tone: “don’t be afraid”, “please don’t shout”.

Other words

  • 1The perfect subjunctive has a long ī (dīxerīs, sīverīs), the future perfect a short i: Bennett; Allen and Greenough §169.d. Ruling: Perfect subjunctive -erīs, future perfect -eris.

    nē1 (+ perfect subjunctive) — don’t (ever) …! (nē dīxerīs)

    nē with the perfect subjunctive, second person · also used · classical · Publil. Sent. (prōsa) T 8: Turpia nē dīxerīs; Quint. 1.5.50: alterum negandī est alterum vetandī

    Firmer: the prohibition of rules and advice. Quintilian counts nōn fēcerīs for nē fēcerīs a fault, “since one denies and the other forbids”.

  • cavē (+ subjunctive) — mind you don’t …, be careful not to …

    imperative of caveō with a bare subjunctive, or with nē · also used · classical · Catull. 50.18: nunc audāx cavē sīs

    (with the bare subjunctive, vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs)

    A warning more than an order; see careful, don’t fall (cavē nē cadās).

  • nē (+ imperative) — don’t …! (nē timē)

    nē with the present imperative · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 1345: Nē timē, voluptās mea.

    (vōx cōmica et poētica: Plaut., Ter., Verg.; not in classical prose)

Examples

  • Ego sum, nōlīte timēre.

    It is I; don’t be afraid.Jo. 6, 20

  • rogō, nōlī clāmāre

    please don’t shoutPetr. 137.1

  • nōlī, inquit, tamquam assem elephantō dēs

    “Don’t,” he said, “do it as if you were giving a penny to an elephant.”Quint. 6.3.59

  • Turpia nē dīxerīs: paulātim enim pudor rērum per verba discutitur

    Never say ugly things: little by little words knock the shame out of things.Publil. Sent. (prōsa) T 8

  • vīcīnīs bonus estō; familiam nē sīverīs peccāre

    be good to your neighbours; don’t let your household do wrongCato Agr. 4

  • nunc audāx cavē sīs

    now mind you aren’t recklessCatull. 50.18

  • Nē timē, voluptās mea.

    Don’t be afraid, my darling.Plaut. Mil. 1345

  • Cavē circumspiciās.

    Don’t look around.Traupman 97, who gives it for “keep your eyes open” (see watch out!)

See also not, don’t touch, careful, don’t fall, ban, want, watch out!.
